label: Act: InAct x r: x actually has the perfection r, as fire is actually hot
definition: `InAct x r`: x actually has the perfection r, as fire is actually hot. In Lean `InAct` is a parameter, not a definition: its content is fixed only by the premises that use it, above all that nothing is in act and in potency in the same respect at once. Whether a mover must have the perfection formally or may have it virtually is left open (DISAMB-IN-ACT).
note: Lean locator: MotionModel.InAct is the field InAct : Being → Respect → Prop, not the whole MotionModel and not a proof of its metaphysical interpretation. The field is a primitive input; the linked premise readings constrain its use but do not define actual possession of a perfection. The match between an intended example and this primitive interpretation remains OPEN.
